units.description: Is p a valid JSON Pointer (RFC 6901)? The text is bytes. true for the empty pointer (the whole document). Otherwise p must start with "/" (byte 47), and every "~" (byte 126) anywhere in it must be followed by "0" or "1"; a "~" that is last, or followed by anything else (including "/"), makes it invalid. A token may be empty, so "/" and "//" are valid. Bytes other than "/" and "~" are never a problem, whatever they are (non-ASCII text such as "é" is fine). It must never panic, on any text. It only decides validity; it does not unescape anything.

units.signature: fn ptr_push_token[&h, &r](heap: &!h Heap, b: buffer.Buffer, token: &r [byte]) -> [heap] buffer.Buffer
units.description: Append one reference token to the pointer text held in b, and hand the buffer back: first the byte "/", then the token escaped, byte for byte: "~" becomes "~0", "/" becomes "~1", every other byte (including non-ASCII bytes) is copied unchanged. The escaping is of the raw token, once: a token "~1" (two bytes) is written "/~01". An empty token appends just "/". b is consumed and the returned Buffer is the same text with the token added; the caller drops it. This is the one place that knows how to escape, to be used by ptr_format and ptr_append.
tests: fn t_same[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var k = 0; while k < len(x) { if x[k] != y[k] { return false; } k = k + 1; } return true; }

fn t_push_is[&h](heap: &!h Heap, start: &static [byte], token: &static [byte], want: &static [byte]) -> [heap] int { var b = buffer.append(heap, buffer.empty(heap, 8), start); b = ptr_push_token(heap, b, token); var same = false; borrow b as &x in { same = t_same(buffer.bytes(x), want); } buffer.drop(heap, b); if same { return 0; } return 1; }
pub fn test_push_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(t_push_is(heap, "", "a/b", "/a~1b"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_push_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(t_push_is(heap, "/x", "~", "/x/~0"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_push_3[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(t_push_is(heap, "", "", "/"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_push_4[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(t_push_is(heap, "", "~1", "/~01"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_push_5[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(t_push_is(heap, "/a", "é", "/a/é"), 0); return 0; }

units.description: Split a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into its unescaped reference tokens, in order: Ok(tokens), or Err(message) if p is not a valid pointer (see ptr_valid). The empty pointer "" is Ok with no tokens. Otherwise p must start with "/", and each "/" starts the next token, which runs to the next "/" or the end: "/a/b" is two tokens, "/" is one empty token, "//" is two empty tokens, "/a/" is "a" then an empty one. Inside a token "~1" stands for "/" and "~0" for "~"; a "~" not followed by 0 or 1 makes the whole pointer an Err, as does a non-empty p that does not start with "/". Unescape each token in one left-to-right pass, so "~01" is the two bytes "~1" (never "/"). Non-ASCII bytes pass through unchanged. It must never panic, on any text. The token list is list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]]: each token is a Box holding a Box of bytes, one more Box than looks needed, because the compiler cannot match a plain Box[[byte]] through a reference (alpibrusl/cancho#461). list.push puts an element at the FRONT, so build the list from the last token to the first. A parsed pointer is owned by the caller, who frees it: this function allocates one boxed byte run per token and one list cell per token.
tests: fn t_same[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var k = 0; while k < len(x) { if x[k] != y[k] { return false; } k = k + 1; } return true; }

fn t_drop[&h](heap: &!h Heap, l: list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]]) -> [heap] int { match l { list.List::Empty => { return 0; } list.List::Cons(f, rest) => { unbox_slice(heap, unbox(heap, f)); let tail = unbox(heap, rest); return 1 + t_drop(heap, tail); } } }

fn t_nth_is[&l, &r](l: &l list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]], idx: int, want: &r [byte]) -> [] bool { match l { list.List::Empty => { return false; } list.List::Cons(f, rest) => { if idx == 0 { return t_same(contents(contents(f)), want); } return t_nth_is(contents(rest), idx - 1, want); } } }

pub fn test_parse_ok_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_parse(heap, "/a~1b") { result.Result::Ok(l) => { var ok = true; borrow l as &r in { if list.length(r) != 1 { ok = false; } if !t_nth_is(r, 0, "a/b") { ok = false; } } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }

pub fn test_parse_ok_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_parse(heap, "/~01") { result.Result::Ok(l) => { var ok = true; borrow l as &r in { if list.length(r) != 1 { ok = false; } if !t_nth_is(r, 0, "~1") { ok = false; } } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }

pub fn test_parse_ok_3[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_parse(heap, "//") { result.Result::Ok(l) => { var ok = true; borrow l as &r in { if list.length(r) != 2 { ok = false; } if !t_nth_is(r, 0, "") { ok = false; } if !t_nth_is(r, 1, "") { ok = false; } } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }

pub fn test_parse_ok_4[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_parse(heap, "/") { result.Result::Ok(l) => { var ok = true; borrow l as &r in { if list.length(r) != 1 { ok = false; } if !t_nth_is(r, 0, "") { ok = false; } } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }

pub fn test_parse_ok_5[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_parse(heap, "") { result.Result::Ok(l) => { var ok = true; borrow l as &r in { if list.length(r) != 0 { ok = false; } } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }

pub fn test_parse_ok_6[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_parse(heap, "/a/b/c") { result.Result::Ok(l) => { var ok = true; borrow l as &r in { if list.length(r) != 3 { ok = false; } if !t_nth_is(r, 0, "a") { ok = false; } if !t_nth_is(r, 1, "b") { ok = false; } if !t_nth_is(r, 2, "c") { ok = false; } } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }

pub fn test_parse_ok_7[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_parse(heap, "/é") { result.Result::Ok(l) => { var ok = true; borrow l as &r in { if list.length(r) != 1 { ok = false; } if !t_nth_is(r, 0, "é") { ok = false; } } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
pub fn test_parse_err_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_parse(heap, "a/b") { result.Result::Ok(l) => { t_drop(heap, l); return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
pub fn test_parse_err_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_parse(heap, "/~") { result.Result::Ok(l) => { t_drop(heap, l); return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }

units.signature: fn ptr_format[&h, &l](heap: &!h Heap, tokens: &l list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]]) -> [heap] buffer.Buffer
units.description: The JSON Pointer for a list of reference tokens: each token escaped ("~" becomes "~0", "/" becomes "~1", everything else unchanged, escaped once and byte for byte) and prefixed with "/", written one after another with nothing between. The empty list gives the empty text "", and a list of one empty token gives "/". The tokens are only borrowed: the caller keeps and frees the list. The result is a heap-owned buffer.Buffer that the caller drops (cancho has no string type). For every list of tokens, ptr_parse of the formatted text gives the same tokens back. The token list is list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]] (each token a Box holding a Box of bytes, as in ptr_parse), and you reach a token's bytes with contents(contents(t)) when t is the element bound by matching a list.List::Cons(t, rest) through a reference.
tests: fn t_same[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var k = 0; while k < len(x) { if x[k] != y[k] { return false; } k = k + 1; } return true; }

fn t_drop[&h](heap: &!h Heap, l: list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]]) -> [heap] int { match l { list.List::Empty => { return 0; } list.List::Cons(f, rest) => { unbox_slice(heap, unbox(heap, f)); let tail = unbox(heap, rest); return 1 + t_drop(heap, tail); } } }
fn t_mk[&h, &r](heap: &!h Heap, s: &r [byte]) -> [heap] Box[[byte]] { let b = box_slice(heap, len(s), byte_of(0)); borrow mut b as &!w in { copy_into(contents(w), s); } return b; }

pub fn test_format_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { var l: list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]] = list.List::Empty; l = list.push(heap, l, box(heap, t_mk(heap, ""))); l = list.push(heap, l, box(heap, t_mk(heap, "c~d"))); l = list.push(heap, l, box(heap, t_mk(heap, "a/b"))); var ok = false; borrow l as &r in { let out = ptr_format(heap, r); borrow out as &q in { ok = t_same(buffer.bytes(q), "/a~1b/c~0d/"); } buffer.drop(heap, out); } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; }

pub fn test_format_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { var l: list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]] = list.List::Empty; l = list.push(heap, l, box(heap, t_mk(heap, ""))); var ok = false; borrow l as &r in { let out = ptr_format(heap, r); borrow out as &q in { ok = t_same(buffer.bytes(q), "/"); } buffer.drop(heap, out); } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; }

pub fn test_format_3[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { var l: list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]] = list.List::Empty; var ok = false; borrow l as &r in { let out = ptr_format(heap, r); borrow out as &q in { ok = t_same(buffer.bytes(q), ""); } buffer.drop(heap, out); } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; }

pub fn test_format_4[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { var l: list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]] = list.List::Empty; l = list.push(heap, l, box(heap, t_mk(heap, "~1"))); var ok = false; borrow l as &r in { let out = ptr_format(heap, r); borrow out as &q in { ok = t_same(buffer.bytes(q), "/~01"); } buffer.drop(heap, out); } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; }

pub fn test_format_5[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { var l: list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]] = list.List::Empty; l = list.push(heap, l, box(heap, t_mk(heap, "é"))); var ok = false; borrow l as &r in { let out = ptr_format(heap, r); borrow out as &q in { ok = t_same(buffer.bytes(q), "/é"); } buffer.drop(heap, out); } t_drop(heap, l); if ok { return 0; } return 1; }

units.signature: fn ptr_append[&h, &r, &t](heap: &!h Heap, p: &r [byte], token: &t [byte]) -> [heap] result.Result[buffer.Buffer, &static [byte]]
units.description: Add one reference token to the end of a pointer: Err(message) if p is not a valid pointer (see ptr_valid; the token is never checked, any bytes are a legal token), otherwise Ok(p followed by "/" followed by the escaped token). p is copied as it is, NOT re-escaped (it is already escaped text); only token is escaped ("~" becomes "~0", "/" becomes "~1"). So appending to "" gives "/token", and appending the empty token to "/a" gives "/a/". The result is a heap-owned buffer.Buffer that the caller drops; on Err nothing is allocated that the caller must free.
tests: fn t_same[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var k = 0; while k < len(x) { if x[k] != y[k] { return false; } k = k + 1; } return true; }

pub fn test_append_ok_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_append(heap, "/a", "x/y") { result.Result::Ok(b) => { var ok = false; borrow b as &x in { ok = t_same(buffer.bytes(x), "/a/x~1y"); } buffer.drop(heap, b); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }

pub fn test_append_ok_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_append(heap, "", "~") { result.Result::Ok(b) => { var ok = false; borrow b as &x in { ok = t_same(buffer.bytes(x), "/~0"); } buffer.drop(heap, b); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }

pub fn test_append_ok_3[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_append(heap, "/a/b", "") { result.Result::Ok(b) => { var ok = false; borrow b as &x in { ok = t_same(buffer.bytes(x), "/a/b/"); } buffer.drop(heap, b); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }

pub fn test_append_ok_4[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_append(heap, "/a~1b", "c") { result.Result::Ok(b) => { var ok = false; borrow b as &x in { ok = t_same(buffer.bytes(x), "/a~1b/c"); } buffer.drop(heap, b); if ok { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
pub fn test_append_err_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_append(heap, "a", "x") { result.Result::Ok(b) => { buffer.drop(heap, b); return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
pub fn test_append_err_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { match ptr_append(heap, "/~", "x") { result.Result::Ok(b) => { buffer.drop(heap, b); return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }

units.description: The pointer to the parent of p: Err(message) if p is not a valid pointer (see ptr_valid) or is the empty pointer (the root has no parent), otherwise Ok(p without its last token), that is p cut at its LAST "/" (the cut drops that "/" and everything after it). Because "~1" is the escape for a slash, the last raw "/" byte is always a token boundary. "/a/b" gives "/a", "/a" gives "" (the root), "/" gives "", and "/a//" gives "/a/". The Ok text is a sub-slice of p itself (p[0..i], the same region &r), so nothing is allocated and nothing needs freeing; the text is not copied or re-escaped.
tests: fn t_same[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var k = 0; while k < len(x) { if x[k] != y[k] { return false; } k = k + 1; } return true; }
pub fn test_parent_ok_1() -> [] int { match ptr_parent("/a/b") { result.Result::Ok(q) => { if t_same(q, "/a") { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
pub fn test_parent_ok_2() -> [] int { match ptr_parent("/a") { result.Result::Ok(q) => { if t_same(q, "") { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
pub fn test_parent_ok_3() -> [] int { match ptr_parent("/") { result.Result::Ok(q) => { if t_same(q, "") { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
pub fn test_parent_ok_4() -> [] int { match ptr_parent("/a//") { result.Result::Ok(q) => { if t_same(q, "/a/") { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
pub fn test_parent_ok_5() -> [] int { match ptr_parent("/a~1b/c") { result.Result::Ok(q) => { if t_same(q, "/a~1b") { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
pub fn test_parent_err_1() -> [] int { match ptr_parent("") { result.Result::Ok(_) => { return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
pub fn test_parent_err_2() -> [] int { match ptr_parent("a") { result.Result::Ok(_) => { return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
pub fn test_parent_err_3() -> [] int { match ptr_parent("/a~") { result.Result::Ok(_) => { return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
